Prenatal testing revenue rose 72% to $96.5M and oncology clinical testing quadrupled to $10.7M, prompting a raised full-year revenue guidance of $450-465M. BLLN also launched Unity Confirm, a non-invasive prenatal confirmation assay.

DSGX reported record Q1 FY2027 results on June 3, with revenue up 15% to $193.6M, net income of $48.5M, and a record adjusted EBITDA of $89.8M. Services revenue made up 93% of the total as global trade intelligence, e-commerce customs entries, and transportation visibility offset a soft freight market. DSGX ended the quarter with $377M in cash.

FJET extended gains on its addition to the Russell 3000 Index effective June 29 - an unusually fast index entry for a December 2025 IPO - and an expanded partnership with Mu-g Technologies on parabolic flight testing tied to a joint response to NASA's Request for Information for Parabolic Flight Services. FJET operates the only commercial fleet of flight-ready F-104 supersonic aircraft. A small post-IPO float amplified the momentum move.

LQDA extended its post-earnings advance as multiple analysts raised price targets, building on Q1 2026 results showing revenue of $132.9M (up from $3.1M a year earlier), net income of $52.9M, and EPS of $0.52 beating the $0.41 consensus - a third straight profitable quarter on YUTREPIA treprostinil economics. Pipeline progress on the Phase 3 Re-Spire trial for L606 and upcoming BofA and H.C. Wainwright healthcare conferences kept the bid underpinned.

MANU surged on reports that members of the Glazer family are exploring a sale of their shares, with potential interest from wealthy Middle East and U.S. buyers at a premium valuation. The ownership-change speculation combined with the club's improving financial trajectory drove the move, though some investors flagged strategic uncertainty around a potential control shift.

MDT reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $9.8B (up 9.9%, 6.6% organic) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.55 ahead of guidance, capping its strongest annual revenue growth in a decade at $36.4B. The board raised the dividend to $0.72/share, its 49th consecutive annual increase, and guided FY27 organic growth of 6.75-7.25%. BTIG upgraded MDT to Buy with a $90 target, citing consistent mid-single-digit organic growth and undervaluation versus peers.

NN jumped after Oppenheimer raised its price target to $50, citing roughly $8B in value for the company's 900MHz spectrum at a $1.50 per MHz-PoP assumption that could climb further in a bidding war. The upgrade refocused attention on NN's spectrum assets and its recent FCC notice of proposed rulemaking for 5G-based 3D positioning in the lower 900MHz band.

TEM rallied after FDA approval of a tumor-only indication for its xT CDx sequencing platform, making it the first lab with companion diagnostic approval for both tumor-only and tumor-normal genomic profiling and flagging an estimated $200 ASP benefit from 2027. TEM also launched the IMS Open-Source digital pathology consortium with Yale New Haven and Memorial Sloan Kettering, and expanded its Bristol Myers Squibb collaboration across five oncology and neuroscience programs. A priced $400M 0% convertible notes deal due 2032 added to the news flow.

2026-06-05.catalyst: ABM reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.90, beating the $0.88 consensus, on record revenue of $2.29B (up 8.4% YoY, 6.1% organic) versus the $2.24B estimate. Growth was led by technical solutions demand tied to the AI data center buildout, the company's fastest growth in nearly four years. ABM reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.85-$4.15, with the midpoint above the $3.96 Street consensus, and guided to a stronger second half.

COO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.082B (up 8%, 5% organic) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.21, up 26% YoY and ahead of consensus, on CooperVision contact lens and CooperSurgical strength. GAAP EPS came in at -$0.40 on a litigation charge to resolve claims tied to a December 2023 CooperSurgical product recall, but the market focused on the non-GAAP beat and organic growth. Results were released after the June 4 close, lifting shares on June 5.

GIII reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $536M, ahead of guidance, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.50 versus $0.17 a year earlier - lifted by a $77.9M net benefit ($1.75/share) from the expected recovery of previously paid IEEPA tariffs. Excluding that item, the non-GAAP net loss of $0.21 still came in ahead of guidance on healthy full-price selling and gross margin expansion across the go-forward owned brands and the Marc Jacobs acquisition. GIII raised full-year FY2027 guidance to EPS of $2.15-$2.25 on revenue of about $2.71B.

2026-06-08.catalyst: GLXY surged on two catalysts: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management launched a referral capability letting eligible clients lend crypto directly to GLXY, and chairman Mike Novogratz said GLXY is building the largest single-campus US data center, a 1.6-gigawatt West Texas site already half-leased. GLXY also opened an institutional OTC trading desk focused on prediction markets. The moves point to more Wall Street flow through GLXY platforms and a deeper push into institutional crypto and AI data center infrastructure.

IDYA jumped after reporting positive Phase 2/3 OptimUM-02 data showing its darovasertib plus crizotinib combination improved progression-free survival and response rates versus standard therapy in first-line HLA-A*02:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma, supporting an expedited NDA filing. The data were presented at ASCO. IDYA also entered a clinical collaboration with Roche pairing its PRMT5 inhibitor IDE892 with Roche pan-RAS inhibitor in MTAP-deleted, RAS-mutant pancreatic cancer, and announced a proposed $300M stock-and-warrant offering.

IFNNY rose with the broad AI-semiconductor demand rally on June 8, with no IFNNY-specific same-day announcement confirmed. AI server infrastructure is expected to make its Power and Sensor Systems division one of its fastest-growing segments. Recent context: IFNNY integrated its OPTIGA Trusted Platform Module with NVIDIA Jetson Thor and guided fiscal 2026 revenue above EUR 16 billion.

KXIAY extended its NAND super-cycle rally as memory undersupply and rising NAND prices boost its pricing power and profitability. Its most recent quarter (Jan-Mar 2026) showed revenue up 189% YoY to JPY 1,002.9B and operating profit up roughly 15x to a record JPY 596.8B, and KXIAY market cap recently surpassed Toyota to rank among Japan most valuable companies. No company-specific same-day catalyst was confirmed; the move tracked the memory-demand wave.

MRVL climbed on accelerating AI data center demand following record Q1 FY27 revenue of $2.418B (up 28% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.80, with Q2 guided to about $2.7B (35% growth) and a raised FY27-28 outlook. A wave of Wall Street upgrades lifted price targets as high as $300, and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang publicly praised the company. Its new Teralynx T100 102.4 Tbps switch positions MRVL deeper inside hyperscale AI clusters.

OSCR rose after presenting at the Goldman Sachs Healthcare Conference on June 8, where management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance and said the year is progressing strongly, citing favorable trends and lighter-than-expected market morbidity. The update reassured investors that the insurer growth and profitability targets remain on track.

TNGX surged to an all-time high after its experimental cancer drug vopimetostat, combined with Revolution Medicine daraxonrasib, achieved a 92% objective response rate in advanced pancreatic cancer, with tumor shrinkage in 11 of 12 patients. TNGX plans to advance the combination into Phase 3. Leerink raised its target to $55, Wolfe upgraded to Outperform, and Wedbush and Mizuho also lifted targets. TNGX separately launched a proposed $500M stock offering.

2026-06-09.catalyst: ADUR jumped after reporting results from its Next Generation Process (NGP) pilot plant, where a 47-hour run achieved 86 percent liquid hydrocarbon recovery with about 85 percent of the liquids in the C20-and-below range tied to naphtha cracker feedstocks. The data strengthens the commercial case for ADUR's chemical recycling technology with petrochemical offtakers. Peers were mixed on the day, pointing to a stock-specific reaction.

ALHC surged after presenting at the Goldman Sachs 47th Annual Global Healthcare Conference, where it highlighted accelerating Medicare Advantage growth and 2025 revenue of $3.95 billion, up 46 percent year over year. The company was also newly named to the Fortune 1000 at No. 791, with founder-CEO John Kao adding the chairman role. Most healthcare peers traded lower, underscoring a stock-specific move.

ASH rallied as activist Standard Investments disclosed a larger position, lifting its economic exposure to nearly 10 percent and intensifying pressure for portfolio streamlining at the specialty chemicals maker. The move follows a recent board refresh that added former Entegris CEO Bertrand Loy. Investors are repricing the odds of value-unlocking restructuring.

BAP rebounded as Peru's presidential runoff gap narrowed to under 20,000 votes with uncounted overseas ballots expected to favor market-friendly Keiko Fujimori, easing the political-risk selloff from the prior session. Fitch's June 8 upgrade of BAP to BBB+ on the strength of Banco de Credito del Peru added support. The move was driven by country political-risk repricing rather than a company event.

2026-06-09.catalyst: CBRL jumped after fiscal Q3 2026 results crushed expectations, with adjusted EPS of $0.29 versus a consensus loss near $0.48 and adjusted EBITDA of $40.3 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.27 to $3.30 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $120 to $125 million, and declared a $0.25 dividend. Comparable sales still fell, but the earnings beat and raised outlook drove the move.

CECO surged after issuing a sharply upgraded full-year 2026 outlook that folds in its recently closed Thermon acquisition, guiding revenue to $1.275 to $1.375 billion, about 20 percent growth at the midpoint, and adjusted EBITDA to $195 to $225 million. The company also flagged record bookings in early June. Shares hit an all-time high on the raise.

CRDO rose after a blowout fiscal Q4 in which revenue of about $437 million grew roughly 157 percent year over year, capping a FY26 where revenue more than tripled to about $1.34 billion and non-GAAP net income jumped more than fivefold. Analysts piled on with price-target hikes, including Jefferies to $270, Mizuho to $290 and Roth to $300. The AI-driven connectivity demand story keeps fueling the run.

GLXY extended its multi-day rally, continuing to ride its push into institutional crypto and AI infrastructure. The firm launched an institutional-scale OTC desk for event-contract prediction markets tied to economic, political and geopolitical outcomes, building on its Morgan Stanley crypto-lending tie-up and its 1.6-gigawatt West Texas data center buildout. Momentum from those catalysts carried into a second session.

HAE gained after BofA Securities upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral and raised its price target to $80 from $72, citing strength in the vascular closure business and steady plasma demand. The call extends a strong run for the blood-management specialist following its Q4 beat last month. The analyst action was the day's primary driver.

NUVL soared after GSK agreed to acquire the company for $10.6 billion, a large premium that values NUVL's late-stage lung cancer pipeline. The deal centers on two potential best-in-class inhibitors, zidesamtinib for ROS1 and neladalkib for ALK, both under FDA review for 2026, with a PDUFA date of November 27, 2026 for the ALK program. The buyout validates NUVL's targeted oncology platform.

SJM jumped after fiscal Q4 results beat, with adjusted EPS of $2.77, up 20 percent, topping the $2.66 consensus on net sales of $2.3 billion, up 6 percent. The company set fiscal 2027 guidance for adjusted EPS of $9.75 to $10.25 and about $1.0 billion of free cash flow. The earnings beat drove the move despite a softer top-line outlook.

VECO climbed after a leading logic chipmaker placed a follow-on order for its NSA500 nanosecond annealing system following a successful evaluation, and the company shipped an NSA500 to a third advanced logic customer for evaluation. Barclays raised its price target to $55. The order momentum points to broadening adoption of VECO's annealing tools at advanced nodes.

VELO rose after announcing a strategic partnership with Aurelia Technologies to embed its metal additive manufacturing into advanced energy and gas-turbine platforms. The deal extends a string of collaborations spanning U.S. Army and Navy defense work and broader aerospace. The partnership reinforces VELO's positioning in mission-critical additive manufacturing.
